context: Al-Ahzab is Madinan and takes its name from the confederates who besieged the city in the fifth year: a coalition of tribes assembled to end the community in a single campaign. The believers dug a trench across the exposed approach and waited through cold, hunger and fear, and the siege broke without a general battle when a wind scattered the camp of the besiegers.

The surah legislates around that siege on matters the community found difficult: the ending of the practice of treating adopted sons as biological ones, the marriage of Zaynab, the conduct of the Prophet's ﷺ household, and the manner in which visitors were to behave in his home. Several of its passages address awkward, specific and human situations by name.
name_story: Named for al-ahzab, the confederates or the combined parties. The naming keeps the siege at the centre, and the surah's opening account of it is unusually vivid: when eyes shifted and hearts reached the throats, and the believers were shaken with a severe shaking.

movements.h: Adoption, and the covenant of the prophets
movements.note: The end of treating adopted sons as sons in lineage, with the instruction to call them by their fathers, and the solemn covenant taken from the prophets.
The siege described from inside: the fear, the hypocrites asking permission to leave, the believers who saw in it only what Allah had promised, and the wind that ended it.
The choice offered to his wives between the world and Allah and His Messenger, the conduct required of them, and the marriage of Zaynab which ended the adoption rule in practice.
Remember Allah with much remembrance, and the description of the Prophet ﷺ as a witness, a bringer of good tidings, a warner, and a lamp giving light.

movements.h: Manners in the house, and the trust
movements.note: The instruction about entering his home and not staying to talk, the command to send blessings upon him, the outer garment, and the closing verses on the trust that the heavens and the earth declined.

themes.d: The account of the siege does not present the believers as unafraid. Eyes shifted, hearts reached the throats, and they were shaken severely, and the surah records that before it records the relief.
There is for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern. The verse sits inside the siege account, so the pattern being praised is his conduct under exactly those conditions.

themes.t: Ending a practice people were attached to
themes.d: The adoption rule was changed in law and then changed in fact through a marriage the Prophet ﷺ found difficult, and the surah addresses the difficulty rather than hiding it.
The closing image of the heavens, the earth and the mountains refusing to carry the trust, and the human being carrying it, frames everything the surah has legislated.

heart: Recited slowly, the siege passage is one of the few places in the Qur'an where a reciter is put inside collective fear rather than shown it from outside. The detail that undoes most people is small: the hypocrites saying our houses are exposed, when their houses were not exposed. The excuse of a frightened person, recorded permanently.

And in the middle of it, verse 21: an excellent pattern for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often. It is not praise offered in a calm moment. It is said about a man digging a trench with his companions on an empty stomach while a coalition assembles to kill them all.

passages.why: An excellent pattern in the Messenger of Allah. Placed inside the account of the siege, so the pattern is his conduct under siege.
When eyes shifted and hearts reached the throats. The Qur'an describing fear without softening it.
Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings upon him. The basis of the salawat every Muslim says.
The heavens, the earth and the mountains declined to carry the trust, and the human being carried it.

connections.why: An-Nur carries the parallel legislation on the household and on entering homes.
Aal Imran treats Uhud as this surah treats the trench, and the two together are the Qur'an's account of the community under arms.

virtue.text: No authentic report establishes a specific merit for reciting Al-Ahzab. Its weight in daily practice comes from one verse, 33:56, which is the basis of the blessings on the Prophet ﷺ that Muslims say in every prayer and at the mention of his name.
